# Prove Adaptive Yang--Mills Block Domination

## Target

For a gauge-invariant Boolean bad-block field exposed in a declared order,
prove for every finite volume, site, and positive-probability history

```text
P(next block is bad | exposed history) <= q,
```

with `q` below the rooted connected-set threshold. Then apply shared-uniform
sequential coupling to dominate the field by independent Bernoulli(`q`).

## Workflow

1. Freeze the regulator, finite volume, boundary conditions, bad-block
   predicate, adjacency graph, exposure order, and retained boundary state.
2. Make every quantifier explicit: the estimate must cover all
   positive-probability histories generated by the chosen exposure, not all
   arbitrary microscopic link conditionings.
3. Define a gauge-covariant good chart or atlas and a charged complement.
   Retain center, boundary-holonomy, orbit, and topological labels needed to
   prevent free frustrated conditionings.
4. On the good channel, prove a finite-time normalized density comparison.
   Include heat-kernel prefactors, chart mass, overlap multiplicity, Haar
   Jacobians, and action-remainder oscillation.
5. On the complement, prove an extensive multi-link action charge. Check that
   the charge is compatible with the good-collar threshold at the same heat
   time; a deterministic charge without a probability estimate is not enough.
6. Combine the channels into a history-uniform conditional ceiling. Track its
   dependence on volume, support size, scale, and boundary type.
7. Verify `exp(alpha) Delta^2 q < 1`. Apply the sequential coupling theorem and
   report the rooted cluster sum `exp(alpha)q/(1-exp(alpha)Delta^2q)`.
8. Prove stability under the next RG exposure only after gauge covariance,
   locality, state/observable transport, and error summability are certified.
9. Mechanize finite geometry, conditional tables, threshold arithmetic, and
   hostile counterexamples. Finish with a frontier audit.

## Mandatory falsifications

- Test the five-identity/one-negative-center staple conditioning; the exposure
  must charge or exclude it without taking an impossible supremum over all
  microscopic boundaries.
- Test continuous incoherent collars. One-link charging by `eta/2` can be
  quantitatively insufficient even when geometrically exact.
- Test chart normalization in the full physical dimension. Pointwise-small
  action remainders do not imply normalized measure comparison.
- Test the two-site law `P(10)=P(01)=1/2`. It satisfies all intersection
  moment bounds at `q=1/2` but is not dominated by Bernoulli(`1/2`).
- Test invalid radii, zero-mass histories, supercritical weights, topology
  labels, and volume dependence.

## Evidence contract

Return:

- the filtration and retained-information schema;
- good/charged conditional inequalities with constants;
- chart-coverage and topology ledgers;
- the adaptive ceiling and connected-set budget;
- an executable counterexample and threshold suite;
- a theorem dependency graph and first unproved implication.

Label the result conditional unless the adaptive estimate is proved for the
complete nonlinear measure uniformly in volume. Never promote finite
domination to repeated RG, continuum existence, Osterwalder--Schrader
reconstruction, or a Hamiltonian mass gap.
